_notes: access_method values: manual_upload | email_notification | rss | public_page | api.
public_page sources are never fetched automatically until allowed_fetch is true AND you have read the site's terms of use.
url_verified false means the URL was written from general knowledge and must be confirmed in a browser before relying on it.

Research pass 2026-11-05: URLs marked url_verified true come from official pages surfaced by web search; portals were not opened from this environment (state sites were not reachable), so confirm once in a browser.

DC sources added 2026-11-06 from web research: OCP eSourcing (notices need registration), DGS OpenGov (free, Follow for amendments), DC Health and DCPS buy through OCP. CBE certification (principal office in DC) gives evaluation preference.
v2.1 (2026-11-06): public_listing access method added, gated by allowed_fetch + robots.txt; DC transparency portal added.

sources.name: eMaryland Marketplace Advantage (eMMA)
sources.notes: Statewide portal (emma.maryland.gov). Training guides describe a 'Public Solicitations' search usable without an account; attachments and bidding need a free vendor registration. Registered vendors pick UNSPSC commodity codes and receive email notices (one state page cites procurements of $15,000 and over). Help desk: emma.helpdesk@maryland.gov. No published terms covering automated access were found, so the bot does not fetch pages; it reads notification emails instead.

sources.name: eMMA email notifications
sources.notes: Register on eMMA, set bid-notification preferences by UNSPSC commodity code (see docs/maryland_procurement_notes.md for the codes to pick), then set IMAP_* in .env so the scanner can read the notices sent to the Vendor Admin / primary contact. Amendments are also emailed ('Notify Commodity Vendors').

sources.name: Baltimore City (CitiBuy)
sources.notes: Bureau of Procurement site with a Supplier Self-Service Portal (how-to guides updated 2026). Many City solicitations are also posted on eMMA (Maryland Procurement Portal). CitiBuy (baltimorecitibuy.org) is the legacy system. Phone (410) 396-5700 per third-party listing.

sources.name: Baltimore County Purchasing
sources.notes: Division of Purchasing uses an OpenGov portal: https://procurement.opengov.com/portal/baltimorecountymd (free registration, email bid notifications, amendments posted there, sometimes within 48 hours of opening). purchasing@baltimorecountymd.gov, 410-887-3880. Subscribe on the portal and forward notices to the IMAP inbox.

sources.name: Montgomery County Office of Procurement
sources.notes: Solicitation Postings page; documents free to download. Responses to IFB/RFP go through BidNet (free 'Limited' registration). County Vendor Registration System (montgomerycountymd.gov/vendorregistration) needed for award/payment and LSBR/MFD certification. County also sends GovDelivery bulletins (content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MDMONTGOMERY) which can be subscribed by email.

sources.name: Prince George's County Office of Central Services
sources.notes: Office of Central Services / Contract Administration & Procurement (1400 McCormick Dr, Suite 300, Largo). Solicitations posted on the CAP website, the SPEED eProcurement platform (SAP Ariba Discovery) and eMMA; advertised Thursdays in Prince George's Post, Enquirer Gazette and Sentinel. Recent custodial/facility solicitations run by the Office of Procurement on behalf of OCS.

sources.name: Anne Arundel County Purchasing
sources.notes: Portal not confirmed by research; verify in a browser. Third-party aggregators list county opportunities.

sources.name: Howard County Purchasing
sources.notes: Solicitations run on PlanetBids (free supplier registration; search, download documents, receive addenda by email).

sources.name: Baltimore City Public Schools Procurement
sources.notes: City Schools solicitations (facilities, custodial, food service, school replacement IFBs) are posted on eMMA; register there and pick the commodity codes.

sources.name: Montgomery County Public Schools Procurement
sources.notes: MCPS Supplier Portal. Must select bid-notification categories after registering or no notices are sent.

sources.name: Prince George's County Public Schools Purchasing
sources.notes: Purchasing & Supply Services; has an MBE program; 2026 business-series slides point vendors to the PGCPS website for opportunities.

sources.name: University System of Maryland institutions
sources.notes: UMD, UMB, UMBC, Towson and others post on eMMA; some also maintain their own procurement pages.

sources.name: University of Maryland Medical System supplier portal
sources.notes: Private non-profit system with public ties; supplier registration rather than public bids. Confirm process before relying on it.

sources.name: Maryland Department of General Services
sources.notes: Facilities maintenance and small construction for state buildings; solicitations appear on eMMA.

sources.name: Example RSS feed (disabled)
sources.notes: Template entry: set feed_url to a procurement RSS/Atom feed a site publishes for this purpose.

sources.name: Carroll County Purchasing (Public Purchase)
sources.notes: Bids handled through the Public Purchase platform (free vendor registration with email notifications).

sources.name: Charles County Procurement (OpenGov + eMMA)
sources.notes: Formal solicitations posted on an OpenGov portal and on eMMA.

sources.name: St. Mary's County Procurement
sources.notes: Formal solicitations over $50,000 go through the county eProcurement portal; site lists an RSS feed link (coverage of bids unconfirmed).

sources.name: BidNet Direct - Maryland purchasing group
sources.notes: Montgomery County and other local agencies accept bids via BidNet. Free 'Limited' registration gives email notifications for the agencies you select; forward them to the IMAP inbox and set IMAP_SENDER_FILTER accordingly.

sources.name: DC Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP)
sources.notes: Central DC procurement for most agencies including DC Health, DCPS and DHS. Solicitations are published in OCP's eSourcing system; vendors must register in eSourcing (one account per tax ID; confirmation can take 24-48 business hours) to receive electronic notifications. Purchase orders flow through the Ariba Supplier Network (may carry fees). Procurement Center of Excellence handles registration questions.

sources.name: DC OCP eSourcing notifications
sources.notes: After eSourcing registration, point its notifications at the scout inbox and add the sender to IMAP_SENDER_FILTER.

sources.name: DC Department of General Services (OpenGov)
sources.notes: DGS runs its own procurement for District facilities: construction, roofing, generators, landscaping and mowing, organics collection, custodial. Since July 2024 all solicitations are on an OpenGov portal; create a free account, 'Follow' solicitations for automatic amendments, and enable notifications. Award data on the Contract Award page.

sources.name: DC DGS OpenGov notifications
sources.notes: OpenGov emails new solicitations and amendments to followers; read through the scout inbox (sender filter 'opengov').

sources.name: DC Health (via OCP)
sources.notes: Pharmacy, immunization, vaccine administration and public-health support contracts are solicited by OCP on DC Health's behalf; grants (RFAs) are separate. Pharmacies can also enroll in the Vaccines for Children program via DC Health.

sources.name: DC Public Schools (via OCP)
sources.notes: Food service, custodial and facilities support for DCPS are solicited through OCP; school modernization through DGS.

sources.name: DC Housing Authority procurement
sources.notes: Independent authority with its own solicitations (maintenance, cleaning, pest control, unit turnover). Verify portal URL in a browser.

sources.name: DC Water procurement
sources.notes: Independent authority; facilities and sanitation-adjacent work. Verify portal URL in a browser.

sources.name: DC Contracts and Procurement Transparency Portal
sources.notes: OCP's public transparency portal for contracts and solicitations (linked from OCP resources). Useful for award history and prime-contractor research; verify URL and terms in a browser.

sources.name: eMMA public solicitations listing (watcher, off by default)
sources.notes: Read-only watcher of the public solicitations search page. Stays OFF until you read eMMA's terms of use; then paste the public listing URL into listing_url and set allowed_fetch true. robots.txt is honored on every run. Untested from the build environment.

sources.name: DC DGS OpenGov public listing (watcher, off by default)
sources.notes: Same rules as above; OpenGov portals are public to view. Set listing_url to the portal's solicitations page once terms are confirmed.
